title: Thrust Reverser Structure — Bolted Strap Repair of a Cracked Upper Spar Cap Run-Out
abstract: Bolted strap repair for a cracked upper spar cap run-out in the thrust reverser structure, used after a crack is found during a scheduled reverser inspection and the unit cannot be exchanged immediately.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the load path across a cracked upper spar cap run-out in the thrust reverser structure by installing a bolted strap, and returns the reverser to service with a defined inspection programme.
sections.damage_assessment: Remove the reverser from the engine and put it on the support stand. Clean the spar cap run-out and remove the sealant. Establish both crack tips by high frequency eddy current and confirm them by dye penetrant. Measure the crack length along the run-out and record the position relative to the cascade attachment. A crack that has reached the cascade attachment land, a crack that has turned into the skin, or a crack accompanied by fretting at the translating sleeve track is outside the scope of this repair. Inspect the strap D5410138344518 and the spar cap NO513931-76 for secondary indications at the same station; an indication in either means the whole run-out must be assessed.
sections.repair_procedure: Drill and ream the crack stop holes at both tips to the diameter on repair drawing RD-54-10-13-914 and confirm by dye penetrant that the tips are captured. Machine the strap seat on the spar cap and prepare the faying surfaces. Apply the protection scheme to all bare material including the crack stop holes. Fit the strap dry and check the gap with a feeler gauge across the whole footprint; shim any gap larger than the drawing value with a laminated shim. Install the anchor nuts AGS522879K5 in the spar cap to the pattern on sheet 2. Install the fasteners wet with sealant, working outwards from the crack stop positions, and torque them in the sequence on sheet 3. Where the strap reaches the cascade attachment, use the shorter fastener given on the drawing and do not encroach on the attachment land. Seal the strap edge and restore the protection scheme. Refit the reverser and do a full deploy and stow cycle before the engine is run.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a high frequency eddy current inspection of both crack stop holes and of the strap perimeter every 2500 flight cycles, with the reverser opened. Do a detailed visual inspection of the strap edge sealant at every cowl opening. Any growth from a crack stop hole, any loose anchor nut, or any indication at the cascade attachment land makes the repair invalid and the reverser must be removed. The repair is life limited to 8000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: A single crack up to 30 millimetres along the spar cap run-out, not reaching the cascade attachment land, not turned into the skin and with no fretting at the translating sleeve track.

repair_drawings.title: Bolted strap, thrust reverser upper spar cap run-out

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows, 32 fasteners, 20 mm pitch, 15 mm edge distance, with the inner row staggered across the run-out
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Repair is life limited to 8000 flight cycles; a repeat high frequency eddy current inspection is required every 2500 flight cycles.
